title: Pennsylvania AI Laws

reading.body:
Pennsylvania's only AI-related law is a resolution asking Congress not to block state AI regulation, not a rule governing AI itself.

HR425 is a statement of position. It urges Congress to suspend efforts to pass a federal moratorium on state-level AI regulation, notes both the benefits and the risks of the technology, and reaffirms the General Assembly's authority to legislate on it. It passed on 2026-09-30 and directs the Chief Clerk to send copies to federal officials and Pennsylvania's congressional delegation. Nothing in it imposes a requirement on any developer, deployer, or user of AI in the state.

The pattern is a state asserting jurisdiction before it has exercised it. Pennsylvania has not yet passed a substantive AI statute, so the resolution is best read as a claim on future authority rather than a description of current rules. For AI specifically, this matters because the federal moratorium debate would determine whether states can set their own terms for data centers, model deployment, and use in state agencies. Pennsylvania has taken a side in that fight without yet writing the terms.

What this does not tell the reader is what Pennsylvania law will actually require. One resolution is not a regulatory regime, and the data covers only enacted laws this site judged relevant to AI, not pending bills, executive orders, or agency guidance. It also says nothing about the compute, buildings, or power that AI scaling depends on, because the resolution does not address them.

Pennsylvania has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Pennsylvania

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • HR425: Urging the United States Congress to suspend any and all efforts to pass Federal legislation that would impose a moratorium on state-level artificial intelligence regulation; recognizing the potential benefits along with the risks of misuse and systemic harm of artificial intelligence; acknowledging the importance of state regulation of such technologies; and reaffirming the Pennsylvania General Assembly's sovereign authority to legislate for the protection of Pennsylvanians. passed 2026-09-30

    This House Resolution urges the United States Congress to suspend efforts to pass federal legislation that would impose a moratorium on state level artificial intelligence regulation. It recognizes both the benefits and risks of artificial intelligence and reaffirms the Pennsylvania General Assembly's sovereign authority to legislate for the protection of Pennsylvanians. It also directs the Chief Clerk to transmit copies to specified federal officials and Pennsylvania's congressional delegation.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Pennsylvania. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
